title: Shoulder localization
prompt: A surgical-neck humeral fracture threatens the nerve supplying deltoid and teres minor. Name that nerve.
explanation: This nerve supplies deltoid and teres minor and is vulnerable beside the surgical neck.
sourceTitle: UAMS: Nerves of the Upper Limb

title: Extensor pathway
prompt: Which terminal brachial-plexus nerve supplies the posterior arm and forearm extensor groups?
explanation: The posterior arm and forearm muscles receive radial innervation.
sourceTitle: UAMS: Nerves of the Upper Limb

title: Intrinsic hand pathway
prompt: Which nerve supplies the palmar and dorsal interossei used for finger adduction and abduction?
hints: It arises from the medial cord.
explanation: Interossei receive ulnar motor fibers; a proximal lesion can impair these finger movements.
sourceTitle: UAMS: Nerves of the Upper Limb

title: Wrist compression
prompt: A structure is compressed beneath the flexor retinaculum with the long finger-flexor tendons. Which nerve is involved?
explanation: The median nerve accompanies flexor tendons through the carpal tunnel.

title: Deep flexor branch
prompt: Which median-nerve branch supplies flexor pollicis longus, pronator quadratus and the lateral half of flexor digitorum profundus?
hints: It is a deep motor branch.
explanation: These deep forearm muscles share the anterior interosseous branch of the median nerve.

title: Arm vessel transition
prompt: The axillary artery crosses the inferior border of teres major. What is its new name?
explanation: At the inferior border of teres major, axillary becomes brachial.
sourceTitle: UAMS: Arteries of the Upper Limb

title: Posterior arm companion
prompt: Which brachial-artery branch follows the radial groove along the humeral shaft?
explanation: The deep brachial artery follows the radial groove and may be injured with humeral shaft trauma.
sourceTitle: UAMS: Arteries of the Upper Limb

title: Palmar circulation
prompt: Which forearm artery normally contributes most of the blood to the deep palmar arch?
explanation: The deep palmar arch is predominantly radial; palmar arterial patterns vary.
sourceTitle: UAMS: Arteries of the Upper Limb

title: Pelvic stabilizers
prompt: Which nerve supplies gluteus medius and minimus, supporting pelvic stability during single-leg stance?
explanation: Gluteus medius and minimus receive the superior gluteal nerve.

title: Sensory route at the knee
prompt: Which femoral-nerve branch supplies the medial leg but does not pass through the adductor hiatus?
explanation: The saphenous nerve supplies medial leg and foot skin and leaves the adductor canal separately.

title: Parent nerve localization
prompt: Both superficial and deep fibular branches are interrupted while the tibial division remains intact. Name their common parent nerve.
explanation: The common fibular division gives rise to superficial and deep fibular nerves.

title: First web-space sensation
prompt: Reduced sensation is isolated to the dorsal first interdigital web space. Which peripheral nerve supplies this patch?
explanation: The first dorsal web space is the characteristic deep fibular cutaneous territory.

title: Eversion pathway
prompt: Which nerve supplies fibularis longus and brevis in the lateral compartment of the leg?
explanation: The superficial fibular nerve innervates the principal lateral-compartment evertors.

title: Inguinal vessel transition
prompt: After the external iliac artery passes deep to the inguinal ligament, what is it called?
hints: The name matches the thigh region.
explanation: The external iliac continues as the femoral artery beneath the inguinal ligament.
sourceTitle: UAMS: Arteries of the Lower Limb

title: Dorsal foot continuation
prompt: Which artery continues the anterior tibial artery beyond the ankle onto the dorsum of the foot?
hints: Think of the dorsal foot pulse.
The name describes the foot surface.
explanation: Anterior tibial becomes dorsalis pedis at the ankle.
sourceTitle: UAMS: Arteries of the Lower Limb

title: Superficial venous return
prompt: Which long superficial vein begins medially in the foot and ultimately drains into the femoral vein?
hints: Distinguish it from the small vein.
explanation: The great saphenous vein drains superficial medial lower-limb territories into the femoral vein.

title: Pericardial passage
prompt: Name the pericardial space immediately posterior to the ascending aorta and pulmonary trunk, anterior to the superior vena cava.
hints: Exclude the recess behind the left atrium.
Its first word describes a crosswise course.
explanation: The transverse sinus separates the arterial outflow from the venous inflow reflections.

title: Inferior pericardial anchor
prompt: Which outer pericardial layer attaches to the central tendon of the diaphragm?
hints: Its first word begins with F.
explanation: Fibrous pericardium anchors the sac to the diaphragm and blends superiorly with great-vessel adventitia.

title: Pleural reflection
prompt: Name the potential pleural space between the apposed costal and diaphragmatic parietal pleura.
explanation: This recess lies where costal parietal pleura reflects onto the diaphragm.

title: Diaphragmatic motor supply
prompt: A teaching model traces C3–C5 motor fibers to the diaphragm. Which named nerve carries them?
hints: The source is the cervical plexus.
It also carries diaphragmatic sensory fibers.
explanation: The phrenic nerve supplies the diaphragm and includes fibers from C3–C5.

title: Thoracoabdominal sympathetic route
prompt: Which named thoracic splanchnic nerve typically carries T5–T9 preganglionic sympathetic fibers toward the celiac ganglion?
hints: It passes through a diaphragmatic crus.
explanation: The greater thoracic splanchnic nerve carries this upper thoracic sympathetic contribution.

title: Anterior cardiac groove
prompt: Which coronary artery branch accompanies the great cardiac vein in the anterior interventricular sulcus?
hints: It comes from the left coronary artery.
explanation: The anterior interventricular artery and great cardiac vein share the anterior interventricular sulcus.

title: Cardiac venous collection
prompt: Name the major venous channel receiving the middle and small cardiac veins before opening into the right atrium.
hints: Look in the posterior coronary groove.
Its first word begins with C.
explanation: The coronary sinus returns most cardiac venous blood to the right atrium.

title: Central lymphatic return
prompt: Which large lymphatic channel usually empties at the junction of the left internal jugular and subclavian veins?
hints: It ascends through the posterior mediastinum.
explanation: The thoracic duct usually ends at the left venous angle; terminal anatomy can vary.

title: Foregut arterial trunk
prompt: Which unpaired aortic branch normally divides into left gastric, splenic and common hepatic arteries?
hints: It lies superior to the SMA.
Its first word begins with C.
explanation: The celiac trunk provides these three principal branches.
sourceTitle: TTUHSC: Duodenum, Pancreas and Liver Tables

title: Hepatic inflow junction
prompt: Name the vein usually formed by union of the superior mesenteric and splenic veins.
hints: It delivers blood to liver sinusoids.
Its first word begins with P.
explanation: The portal vein receives major intestinal and splenic venous drainage.
sourceTitle: TTUHSC: Duodenum, Pancreas and Liver Tables

title: Pancreatic head supply
prompt: The inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery arises from which unpaired aortic branch?
hints: It lies inferior to the celiac origin.
explanation: This SMA branch anastomoses with superior pancreaticoduodenal branches around the pancreatic head.
sourceTitle: TTUHSC: Duodenum, Pancreas and Liver Tables

title: Biliary confluence
prompt: The cystic duct joins the common hepatic duct. Name the resulting duct.
hints: It often joins the main pancreatic duct.
explanation: The common bile duct receives hepatic and gallbladder drainage.

title: Deep inguinal entrance
prompt: Which opening in transversalis fascia lies lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels?
explanation: The deep ring is an opening in transversalis fascia lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels.

title: Hernia landmark
prompt: Which named vessels separate the usual medial direct and lateral indirect inguinal hernia routes?
hints: Look at the lateral umbilical fold.
They ascend from the external iliac region.
explanation: Direct inguinal hernias lie medial and indirect routes lateral to these vessels.

title: Medial abdominal weak area
prompt: Name the triangle bounded by rectus abdominis, inferior epigastric vessels and inguinal ligament.
hints: It is associated with direct hernias.
explanation: This triangle is the usual weak area traversed by a direct inguinal hernia.

title: Hindgut arterial source
prompt: Which unpaired aortic branch supplies descending colon, sigmoid colon and the superior rectum?
hints: It gives left colic and sigmoid branches.
explanation: The IMA supplies these hindgut territories through colic, sigmoid and superior rectal branches.

title: Perineal nerve route
prompt: Which nerve exits below piriformis, hooks around the ischial spine and enters the perineum through the lesser sciatic foramen?
explanation: The pudendal nerve takes this indirect route from pelvis to perineum.

title: Sacral parasympathetic route
prompt: Name the S2–S4 nerves carrying preganglionic parasympathetic fibers toward pelvic viscera and distal colon.
hints: Distinguish them from sacral sympathetic branches.
They join the inferior hypogastric plexus.
explanation: These nerves provide the sacral parasympathetic outflow.

title: Anorectal sling
prompt: Which part of levator ani forms a muscular sling around the anorectal junction?
hints: Its name joins pubis and rectum.
explanation: The puborectalis sling helps maintain the anorectal angle.

title: Crossing near the cervix
prompt: Which urinary tube passes inferior to the uterine artery in the pelvis?
explanation: The pelvic ureter passes beneath the uterine artery, an important operative relationship.

title: Left ovarian venous return
prompt: Into which vein does the left ovarian vein normally drain?
hints: The right counterpart drains to the IVC.
Think of the left kidney vessel.
explanation: Left ovarian drainage usually enters the left renal vein; variants occur.

title: Urethral erectile covering
prompt: Which midline erectile body encloses the spongy urethra?
hints: Distinguish it from paired cavernous bodies.
It expands distally into the glans.
explanation: The corpus spongiosum surrounds the penile urethra.

title: Fascial perineal channel
prompt: What canal in obturator internus fascia transmits the pudendal neurovascular bundle?
hints: Look along the lateral perineal wall.
It is also named for Alcock.
Its first word begins with P.
explanation: The pudendal canal is formed in fascia over obturator internus.

title: Voluntary anal sphincter branch
prompt: Which pudendal-nerve branch provides major motor innervation to the external anal sphincter?
hints: Choose the branch toward the anus.
explanation: Inferior rectal branches innervate the voluntary external anal sphincter.

title: Lateral gaze pathway
prompt: Which cranial nerve supplies lateral rectus for abduction of the eye?
explanation: The abducens nerve supplies lateral rectus.

title: Tongue motor pathway
prompt: Which cranial nerve supplies most intrinsic and extrinsic tongue muscles, excluding palatoglossus?
hints: This is principally a motor nerve.
explanation: Hypoglossal innervation serves tongue muscles except palatoglossus, which receives vagal fibers.

title: Thoracic loop
prompt: Which left vagal branch loops beneath the aortic arch before ascending toward the larynx?
hints: It returns upward in the neck.
Its first two words are Left recurrent.
explanation: The left recurrent laryngeal nerve loops under the aortic arch near the ligamentum arteriosum.

title: Vocal tension exception
prompt: Which vagal branch supplies cricothyroid, unlike the recurrent supply to other intrinsic laryngeal muscles?
acceptedAnswers: External branch of superior laryngeal nerve
explanation: The external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve supplies cricothyroid.

title: Opening the vocal folds
prompt: Which intrinsic laryngeal muscle is the sole abductor of the vocal folds?
explanation: Posterior cricoarytenoid rotates the arytenoids to abduct the vocal folds.

title: Mandibular passage
prompt: Through which sphenoid opening does the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve leave the cranial cavity?
hints: Look in the middle cranial fossa.
It lies near rotundum and spinosum.
Its second word begins with O.
explanation: V3 traverses foramen ovale.

title: Meningeal arterial passage
prompt: Which sphenoid opening transmits the middle meningeal artery?
hints: Look in the middle cranial fossa.
explanation: The middle meningeal artery enters through foramen spinosum.

title: Airway posterior relation
prompt: At the root of the neck, which digestive tube lies posterior to the trachea?
hints: Trace the pharynx toward the stomach.
Its upper continuation begins near C6.
explanation: The cervical esophagus lies posterior to the trachea.

title: Crossing visual fibers
prompt: A midline lesion interrupts the crossing nasal-retinal fibers from both eyes. Which structure contains that crossing?
hints: It lies superior to the pituitary region.
Its second word begins with C.
explanation: Nasal retinal axons cross in the optic chiasm; midline compression can impair temporal visual fields.

title: Crossed touch pathway
prompt: After dorsal-column fibers synapse and cross in the medulla, what ascending tract carries them toward the thalamus?
hints: This segment is in the brainstem.
explanation: The medial lemniscus carries crossed dorsal-column pathway information toward the thalamus.

title: Crossed pain pathway
prompt: Which major ascending tract carries body pain and temperature after crossing within the spinal cord?
hints: Its name joins spinal cord and thalamus.
explanation: Spinothalamic fibers cross in the cord and ascend contralaterally; exact deficits depend on lesion extent.

title: Light-reflex input
prompt: Which cranial nerve carries the afferent signal from the illuminated retina in the pupillary light reflex?
explanation: Retinal input reaches the reflex pathway through the optic nerve.

title: Light-reflex output
prompt: Which cranial nerve carries preganglionic parasympathetic fibers toward the ciliary ganglion for pupillary constriction?
explanation: Oculomotor parasympathetic fibers reach the ciliary ganglion before the iris sphincter.

title: Motor crossing
prompt: Name the caudal medullary landmark where most corticospinal fibers cross to form the lateral corticospinal tract.
hints: The crossing lies near the spinal border.
explanation: Most corticospinal axons cross at the pyramidal decussation before descending in the opposite lateral cord.

title: Lateral motor territory
prompt: A teaching lesion involves lateral motor cortex for the contralateral face and upper limb. Which major cerebral artery supplies this region?
hints: Compare lateral and medial cortical surfaces.
The leg region is mainly another territory.
explanation: MCA territory includes lateral face and upper-limb motor cortex; individual deficits vary.

title: Medial motor territory
prompt: Which major cerebral artery supplies medial motor cortex representing the contralateral lower limb?
hints: It courses near the longitudinal fissure.
explanation: ACA territory includes the medial lower-limb motor representation.

title: Front-and-back division
prompt: A reconstructed image divides the body into anterior and posterior portions. Name its anatomical plane.
explanation: A coronal plane separates anterior and posterior portions.

title: Left-and-right division
prompt: A vertical section separates left and right portions without necessarily producing equal halves. Name the plane.
hints: Only a midline example is median.
explanation: Sagittal planes divide left from right; midsagittal specifies equal halves.

title: Superior-and-inferior division
prompt: An image shows a horizontal body section dividing superior from inferior portions. Name its anatomical plane.
hints: It is perpendicular to the long axis.
explanation: A transverse plane separates superior and inferior portions.

title: Roots below the cord
prompt: Name the bundle of descending lumbar and sacral nerve roots below the conus medullaris.
hints: These are roots, not spinal cord.
They lie within the lumbar cistern.
The Latin name means horse tail.
explanation: The cauda equina consists of descending spinal nerve roots below the cord.
sourceTitle: TTUHSC: Back and Spinal Cord Tables

title: CSF-containing spinal space
prompt: Which meningeal space contains cerebrospinal fluid between arachnoid and pia mater?
explanation: CSF occupies the subarachnoid space around the spinal cord and its roots.
sourceTitle: TTUHSC: Back and Spinal Cord Tables

title: Lamina-to-lamina support
prompt: Which elastic spinal ligament bridges the laminae of adjacent vertebrae?
hints: It forms part of the canal wall.
The name refers to yellow coloration.
Its second word begins with F.
explanation: Ligamenta flava connect adjacent vertebral laminae.
sourceTitle: TTUHSC: Back and Spinal Cord Tables

title: Spinal nerve exit
prompt: Name the opening between adjacent vertebral pedicles through which a spinal nerve passes.
hints: Distinguish it from the central canal.
explanation: Adjacent pedicle notches form an intervertebral foramen for spinal nerve passage.

title: Upper cervical pivot
prompt: Which projection of the axis provides the pivot around which the atlas rotates?
hints: It projects superiorly from the body.
The alternative name is odontoid process.
explanation: The dens articulates with the anterior atlas and permits atlantoaxial rotation.
